parsed.notes: Reviewed all five inventory assertions using only disclosed files. No quote_fidelity, pincite, or black_letter rows were present in group_inventory.jsonl.

reasons: The lake record is verified and identifies the case as Pennsylvania v. Muniz, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1990-06-18.
The lake citation fields match the page: official citation 496 U.S. 582, parallel citations 110 S. Ct. 2638 and 110 L. Ed. 2d 528, and vendor citation 1990 U.S. LEXIS 3211.

defect.evidence_quote: JUSTICE BRENNAN delivered the opinion of the Court, except as to Part III-C.
defect.problem: The holding overstates the routine-booking-question rationale as a Court holding. The slurring and sixth-birthday clauses are supported, but Part III-C was expressly excluded from the opinion of the Court; four Justices concurred in the booking-question result for a different reason, and Justice Marshall rejected the exception.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise the final clause to say that the first seven booking answers were admissible, but that the routine-booking-question exception was Justice Brennan's Part III-C plurality rationale, not a majority holding of the Court.

reasons: Text supports the slurring clause: the opinion says slurring and lack of muscular coordination are nontestimonial components and do not, without more, compel a testimonial response.
Text supports the sixth-birthday suppression clause: the opinion says Muniz's response was testimonial and should have been suppressed.

Text does not support treating the routine-booking-question exception as a Court holding because Part III-C was not the opinion of the Court, and the Rehnquist concurrence states it agreed with the result for a different reason.
residual_risks: A narrower statement about admissibility of the first seven booking answers would stand.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Separate the admissibility result from the noncontrolling routine-booking-exception rationale.

reasons: The opinion directly applies Miranda to custodial questioning and discusses when unwarned statements must be suppressed.
The opinion refines Miranda/Innis analysis in the DUI booking context, including testimonial versus physical evidence and custodial-interrogation boundaries.
The lake record shows Supreme Court status and substantial progeny, supporting the 'Key - Progeny / Refinement' role.
residual_risks: The home-role label is editorial, but it is supported by the disclosed opinion text and lake progeny data.

reasons: The authority-weight label is supported by the lake identity fields: court is U.S. Supreme Court and court_level is scotus.
No treatment/currency merits finding is made under lens A.
residual_risks: Treatment/currency review belongs to lens B.

defect.evidence_quote: I agree with the conclusion in Part III-C that the seven "booking" questions should not be suppressed, I do so for a reason different from that of JUSTICE BRENNAN.
defect.locator_note: treatment.scope_note; support wording inside scope note
defect.problem: The treatment scope note repeats the support overclaim that the routine biographical booking questions fall within a routine-booking-question exception as though that were a controlling holding. This is a support-scope defect, not a treatment/currency finding.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep the treatment fields if lens B approves them, but revise the scope note to state that the case is fractured and that the seven booking answers were admissible; Part III-C's routine-booking-exception rationale was plurality-only.

reasons: The lake treatment fields match the content treatment fields, and lens A does not assess good-law currency.
The support language inside the scope note needs narrowing because Part III-C was not the opinion of the Court.
residual_risks: Treatment/currency merits remain for lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'seven booking answers were admissible; Brennan plurality used a routine-booking rationale' instead of stating the exception as the case holding.
